did.unittitle: John F. James and Sons scrapbook
did.abstract: A scrapbook of clippings relating to the Brooklyn real estate business John F. James and Sons.

acqinfo.head: Immediate Source of Acquisition
acqinfo.p: Source and date of acquisition unknown. The scrapbook was found in collection and processed in 2026.

arrangement.head: Arrangement
arrangement.p: The scrapbook pages are housed in a single folder and arranged in the order in which they were found, which is roughly chronological. Some of the pages were detached from the binding at the time of processing and may not have been in their exact original order.

bioghist.head: Historical note
bioghist.p: The real estate firm John F. James and Sons was established in 1858 by John F. James Sr. and located at 193 Montague Street in Brooklyn Heights. John F. James II, its longtime president, was born in Brooklyn in 1881 and joined his father's company not long after graduating from the Brooklyn Polytechnic Institute in 1895. He was a charter member of the Brooklyn Real Estate Board and in 1925 was elected as first president of the Kings County Real Estate Corporation. James was also active in the Flatbush Merchants Association, South Brooklyn Board of Trade, and Prospect Heights Citizens Association. He had two sons, Harold and John, Jr. He passed away in 1933 and was interred at Cypress Hills Cemetery.

list.head: Sources:
list.item: "J.F. James is Dead; Brooklyn Realtor." The New York Times, March 28, 1933, p. 20.

prefercite.head: Preferred Citation
prefercite.p: Identification of item, date (if known); John F. James and Sons scrapbook, CBHM.0044, Box and Folder number; Brooklyn Public Library, Center for Brooklyn History.

processinfo.head: Processing Information
processinfo.p: This scrapbook was found in collection and processed by Dee Bowers in September 2026. At that time, the scrapbook was in very poor condition and could not be safely handled, with most of the pages detached from the binding. The pages were photocopied and the originals discarded. Three non-clipping original items were retained: a black and white photograph, a typed sheet detailing various real estate ad placements, and an oversize auction notice.

relatedmaterial.head: Related Materials
relatedmaterial.p: Brooklyn Real Estate Board magazines and bulletins (ARC.177)
Brooklyn, Queens, and Long Island real estate brochure collection (ARC.296)
Many of the clippings are from the Brooklyn Eagle, which can be found digitally on CBH's Brooklyn Newsstand database.

scopecontent.head: Scope and Contents
scopecontent.p: A scrapbook of clippings, along with some ephemera and one photograph, relating to the Brooklyn real estate business John F. James and Sons. The clippings cover real estate sales and devlopment news in Brooklyn and Long Island, as well as advertisements for various properties, many in Brooklyn Heights. There are many advertisements for Grace Court Chambers (2 Grace Court) on the site of the former Packer mansion, for which John F. James and Sons operated as renting agent. Other properties covered in the clippings include the Seth Low mansion, Hotel Margaret, Van Anden, Royal Castle, Temple Bar building, Livingston Court, Brooklyn Citizen building, Hotel Touraine, and Prentice mansion.
The single photograph in the collection is an 8x10-inch black-and-white print of the Pershing apartment building, located on Union Street east of Franklin Avenue (1038 Union Street).

The oversize auction notice, housed separately, is for the 1916 sale of 115 lots on Ocean Avenue, Avenues U and V, East 21st Street (Kenmore Place), and Neck Road. It includes a detailed map of the lots on offer.
